soapr

soapr is a modern SOAP client and R package generator driven by WSDL definitions. Use it either to generate standalone, type-safe R packages from a WSDL file/URL or to interact dynamically with SOAP 1.1 and SOAP 1.2 web services at runtime.

Features

  • Static Client Generation (Generator): Generates standalone R packages (httr, xml2, R6, bit64 only) with Client and TypeFactory R6 classes, Roxygen documentation, NAMESPACE, and LICENSE.
  • Dynamic Runtime Client (Service / Client): Connects to services directly from a WSDL path or URL for ad-hoc exploration and scripting.
  • Comprehensive WSDL & XSD Support (WSDLParser): Parses multi-schema <wsdl:types>, resolves local and remote <xsd:import> / <xsd:include> chains with cycle protection, and supports recursive <xsd:complexContent> inheritance, <xsd:simpleContent>, <xsd:sequence> / <xsd:choice> / <xsd:all> compositors, and inline anonymous nested types.
  • SOAP 1.1 & SOAP 1.2 Protocol Parity: Automatically selects SOAP 1.1 (http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/, text/xml; charset=utf-8, SOAPAction) or SOAP 1.2 (http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope, application/soap+xml; charset=utf-8; action="...") per port binding and parses SOAP 1.1 / 1.2 faults uniformly across dynamic and static clients.
  • Type Safety & XSD Conversion: Typed constructors, match.arg() validation for enums, xsd:date (Date), UTC xsd:dateTime (POSIXct with timezone offset normalization), xsd:long (bit64::integer64), xsd:boolean, and namespace-compliant elementFormDefault / attributeFormDefault serialization.
  • WS-Security & Mockable Transports: Built-in WSSecurity UsernameToken headers and injectable transport hooks for offline unit testing.
  • Lean Dependency Footprint: Base-R and minimal XML/HTTP dependencies (soapr avoids data-frame/tabular tidyverse packages; generated packages require only httr, xml2, R6, and bit64).

Installation

Install the development version of soapr from GitHub with:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("zachzIAM/soapr", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Note: Pass build_vignettes = TRUE (with pandoc available) if you want to build and view vignettes locally.

Quick Start

1. Static Client Package (Recommended)

Generate a dedicated, standalone R package for your SOAP service with custom package metadata:

library(soapr)

wsdl_url <- "http://www.dneonline.com/calculator.asmx?WSDL"
wsdl <- WSDLParser$new(wsdl_url)

gen <- Generator$new(wsdl)
gen$generate_package(
  path = ".",
  package_name = "calculator",
  author = "Package Maintainer",
  email = "maintainer@example.com",
  license_holder = "Example Org"
)

Install or load the generated package and call operations directly:

devtools::install("calculator")
library(calculator)

client <- calculator::new_client()
result <- client$Add(intA = 5L, intB = 10L)
result$AddResult
#> [1] 15

2. Dynamic Runtime Client

Use Service$new() when you want to inspect and call a service without generating a package on disk:

library(soapr)

svc <- Service$new("service.wsdl")

# Create a typed input object from the schema
req <- svc$factory$create("OrderRequest", Id = bit64::as.integer64("9007199254740993"))

# Invoke an operation
res <- svc$client$SubmitOrder(Payload = req)

For lower-level control, Client$new(wsdl, port_def = ..., factory = ..., transport = ...) accepts a pre-parsed WSDLParser, selected port definition, and custom transport function.

Protocol, Schema & Type Features

Multiple Services, Ports & SOAP 1.1 / 1.2

WSDLs that expose multiple services or both SOAP 1.1 and SOAP 1.2 ports can be targeted explicitly in both dynamic and static clients:

# Inspect discovered services, ports, and SOAP versions (1.1 vs 1.2)
parser <- WSDLParser$new("multiport.wsdl")
names(parser$get_services())

# Dynamic client selecting service and port
svc12 <- Service$new(
  "multiport.wsdl",
  service_name = "CountryInfoService",
  port_name = "CountryInfoServiceSoap12"
)

# Generated static client selecting service and port
client12 <- mypkg::new_client(
  service = "CountryInfoService",
  port = "CountryInfoServiceSoap12"
)

When using a SOAP 1.2 port, soapr automatically wraps payloads in the SOAP 1.2 envelope (http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope) and sets Content-Type: application/soap+xml; charset=utf-8; action="...".

Complex Types, Enums, simpleContent, Dates & Qualified Schemas

  • Complex types (client$types / svc$factory$create): Create nested structures and XML attributes cleanly; generated constructors track soap_type, soap_attrs, and (for <xsd:simpleContent>) soap_simple_content (value text plus attributes).
  • Enumerations: Simple type restrictions generate match.arg() checks in static factories and runtime validation in Client.
  • Dates & DateTimes: xsd:date values parse to Date; xsd:dateTime values (including Z and numeric offsets such as +02:00) normalize to UTC POSIXct.
  • Qualified Namespaces & Attributes: Serializers respect per-WSDL elementFormDefault (qualified vs unqualified) and attributeFormDefault (tns: attribute qualification vs unqualified attributes).
# Static TypeFactory usage with attributes, enums, and dates
amount <- client$types$MoneyAmount(currency = "EUR", value = 42.50)
order <- client$types$Order(
  Priority = "HIGH",
  OrderDate = as.Date("2025-03-10"),
  Amount = amount
)
client$CreateOrder(Order = order)

Authentication (WS-Security)

Attach a UsernameToken SOAP header to either a dynamic client or a generated static client:

sec_header <- WSSecurity$new()$username_token(
  username = "myuser",
  password = "mypassword",
  password_type = "PasswordText"
)
client$add_header(sec_header)

Mock Transport Testing

Inject custom transports in unit tests to inspect outgoing XML envelopes/headers and return mocked HTTP responses offline:

mock_httr_response <- function(url, xml_body, ct = "text/xml; charset=utf-8") {
  headers <- list(`Content-Type` = ct)
  structure(
    list(
      url = url,
      status_code = 200L,
      headers = headers,
      all_headers = list(list(status = 200L, version = "HTTP/1.1", headers = headers)),
      content = charToRaw(enc2utf8(xml_body))
    ),
    class = "response"
  )
}

# Static client mock transport
stat_client <- mypkg::new_client(
  transport = function(url, action, body, config, handle) {
    mock_httr_response(url, "<soap:Envelope ...>...</soap:Envelope>")
  }
)

# Dynamic client mock transport
svc <- Service$new("service.wsdl")
svc$client$transport <- function(url, handle, body, ...) {
  mock_httr_response(url, "<soap:Envelope ...>...</soap:Envelope>")
}
